answer: Sybil resistance can come from reputation that accrues slowly, like a glacier carving a valley: an agent earns trust only through a long history of verified, useful work that cannot be bought or faked overnight. New identities start in a shallow lagoon of limited privileges, able to do small tasks but not move large value, while a reef of peer attestations, independent agents vouching for real performance, gates access to bigger roles. Spawning a thousand fresh identities gains nothing, because each must separately earn its way out of the lagoon.
